title: Panthers Win a Seven-Goal Game They Barely Deserved
dek: Florida's Tkachuks lit up Columbus, Toronto stole one from Colorado, and Philadelphia keeps losing for reasons the chances confirm.
text:
## The game that said everything

The week's best game was Florida 7, Columbus 3 on October 13, and it was stranger than the score. The Panthers had the lopsided final, but the chances were close: FLA generated 3.9 expected goals to CBJ's 3.38, and replaying every shot gives Florida only a 49% chance of winning. A seven-goal night came out of what was nearly a coin flip.

The Tkachuk family did the damage. Brady Tkachuk scored a hat trick in that game, then added another on October 15, and Matthew Tkachuk was named the game's star. Brady has six goals in four games on 2.1 expected goals, so that finishing rate is running well ahead of the chances. Matthew has one goal and seven assists, Seth Jones has eight assists, and the Panthers trio all sit at eight points for the week. Matthew's point streak is at seven games. Sam Bennett had 1.5 expected goals across four games without scoring, a reminder that Florida's luck cuts both ways.

## Steals, rouTs and a snap shot from nowhere

The biggest heist came on opening night of the week. Toronto beat Colorado 6-3 on October 10 while generating 3.15 expected goals to Colorado's 4.61. TOR's win was deserved only 18% of the time, and William Nylander was the star, reaching 700 career points along the way. Colorado's Nathan MacKinnon still finished with eight points, but Nazem Kadri piled up 2.4 expected goals across four games without a goal.

The most one-sided game that actually went the right way was Edmonton 3, San Jose 1, where the Oilers deserved to win 77% of the time. Connor McDavid was the star and played his 800th game.

The least likely goal of the week: Shakir Mukhamadullin's snap shot for Edmonton against Utah on October 15, a 0.4% chance. Brett Howden's tip-in for Vegas (0.9%) and Teuvo Teravainen's wrister for Chicago (1.1%) followed.

## Who owned the week

Kirill Kaprizov led the league with 10 points in four games, including six goals, and the chances mostly back him: 4.5 expected goals of his own. Minnesota's Matt Boldy had a hat trick and five goals overall, and Mark Stone (VGK), Kirill Marchenko (TOR) and Brandon Hagel (TBL) also had hat tricks.

In goal, Detroit's Daniil Tarasov stopped 47 of 48 shots across two games (.979), worth 5.1 goals saved above expected. At the other end, Ottawa's Samuel Ersson allowed seven goals on 26 shots (.731, minus 3.6 goals saved above expected) in his one start.

Edmonton's scoring has a regression warning attached. Evan Bouchard has six goals on 1.1 expected, shooting 24%. Vasily Podkolzin has seven on 4.3 expected, shooting 32% against 14% last season. McDavid's team has scored 8.9 more goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice, so his 18 points are padded by on-ice luck. On the other side, Buffalo's Ryan McLeod, the Rangers' Pavel Dorofeyev and Calgary's Simon Nemec are all due for a swing back.

## Up and down

Carolina has won six straight, outscoring opponents 29-13, and the chances back it with 63% of the expected goals. Mark Jankowski has scored in five straight games and Sebastian Aho has a seven-game point streak. Boston (15-6 on the week, three wins) has won four straight, but with only 50% of the expected goals; the goaltending has saved 5.9 goals above expected. Utah also went 3-0-0, and Vegas leads the standings at 7-2-0 with 14 points.

At the bottom, Philadelphia is winless in nine (0-6-3), outscored 33-11, with 37% of the expected goals. That is real. Vancouver is winless in six with 38%, also real. Los Angeles is 0-3-2, but its 51% share suggests mostly bad luck. Calgary sits at 1-6-0. Remember it is early: about eight games in, so chances tell us more than goals.

## Milestones and moves

Milestones: Sean Monahan played his 900th game, Blake Coleman his 700th, and Nico Hischier scored his 200th career goal. Ilya Mikheyev reached 100 career goals, Carson Soucy 100 career points, and Podkolzin 50 career goals.

On October 15, Toronto placed forward Miles Wood on injured reserve and acquired forward Aatu Räty from Vancouver for forwards Brandon Buhr and Jacob Quillan. Räty has one goal in four games with the Canucks, whose team has taken only 28.1% of the expected goals at five-on-five with him on the ice. Toronto is 3-3-2 with 44.6% of the expected goals overall. In Los Angeles, the Kings placed Alex Turcotte and Mats Zuccarello on injured reserve and agreed to a two-year, $1.85 million deal with right wing Jared Wright.
